jobs.name: port-serein
jobs.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: visual direction study for Veyra, a futuristic sci-fi RPG inspired by the lived-in atmosphere of Anarchy Online.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: an actual screenshot freshly captured from the current game.
Create one full-frame landscape edited screenshot, preserving the input aspect ratio. Preserve its exact camera angle, horizon position, geography, distant mountains, lighting direction and time of day, and most of the existing landscape. Work directly onto this screenshot, not a newly imagined landscape. Remove the debug HUD in the upper left, filling it with the matching scene.
Visual language: believable, inviting far-future civilization. Pale mineral concrete and ivory composite shells with softly rounded corners, strong chunky silhouettes, inset charcoal mechanical assemblies, muted petrol-teal cladding and small warm oxidized-orange utility accents. Distinctive modular construction with legible entrances, human-scale details and functional infrastructure. Restrained cyan/amber status lights visible only where useful. Architecture should feel built and maintained over generations, with slight weathering and individual additions. Match the game's clear 3D-rendered environment, existing sun and cast shadows; added structures should be convincing game art and integrate into the existing screenshot. Preserve the existing terrain/vegetation rendering instead of replacing it with a photoreal landscape.
Constraints: no title, no border, no collage, no watermark, no explanatory labels. No fantasy portals, floating islands, glowing energy beams, pervasive neon, ruined apocalypse or generic glass skyscraper skyline. Keep the terrain outside the construction footprints unchanged.
Scene: Port Serein, an inhabited futuristic coastal city.
The original screenshot has open water on the left, a beach curving from the bottom right towards the center-right horizon, and a mountain ridge in the right distance. Keep these recognizable exactly.
Build a substantial but compact city along the RIGHT coastal slope and middle distance, leaving the left sea and much of the foreground beach exposed. Terraced clusters of 4-8-storey apartment and commercial blocks climb the slope, with 2 or 3 taller distinctive civic structures creating a memorable skyline. Architecture blends broad chamfered rectangular masses, curved balcony ends, shaded arcades, turquoise composite panels, inset windows and rooftop gardens. An elevated civilian transit line follows the settlement contour on practical supports. A modest working harbor with piers meets the existing shoreline; service cranes, a few cargo vessels and a small shuttle apron are integrated at credible scale. Show a walkable waterfront with shade structures and a few tiny residents for scale. One or two compact freight skimmers may approach the port. The city belongs to a functioning frontier society and should look like somewhere people can live, shop, work and arrive. Maintain the coast shape and the original blue sky; distinguish the city through architecture rather than changing the weather or color grading.

Scene: a monumental atmospheric processor and its service settlement in the Serein Basin.
The original screenshot is an open dry grass plain with scattered small trees and a jagged mountain ridge along the right horizon. Preserve that landscape and its exact viewpoint.
Place the principal atmospheric processor in the open central-left middle ground, well clear of the right-hand mountain ridge. It is a physically supported, roughly 120-metre-tall terraforming machine: a massive vertically ribbed cylindrical intake body carried by three thick splayed structural buttresses, stacked louvered heat-exchange fins and accessible maintenance galleries. A tapered instrument mast extends from the crown. Clearly engineered volumes and readable silhouettes, not a decorative ring or a conventional nuclear cooling tower. Pale shell panels are interrupted by dark intake slots, teal service enclosures and sparse orange access parts. Deep mechanical shadows, massive footings, believable load paths, only a faint trace of vapor.
At its base, add a small operational campus of workshops, switchgear and utility buildings at approximately 3-10 metres tall, giving an unmistakable scale comparison. An unpaved service road curves from the lower-right foreground towards the machine, with intermittent buried-conduit access covers, a roadside relay box, a small service vehicle and two tiny workers near the base. Leave most of the plain open, preserving its existing scattered trees outside the construction areas. Human habitation and maintaining the planet must read together. Keep the original clear daytime sky.

Scene: a small independent frontier service settlement grown among the woodland.
Preserve the original ground-level forest view, especially the large foreground trunk just right of center, the slim trees on the left, the branching tree silhouettes, the distant treeline and existing foreground flowers and shadows. Keep the large foreground trees as occluders in front of the new structures.
Insert a cluster of 5-7 small one- and two-storey buildings into the middle ground BETWEEN the trunks, 20-60 metres away. Use elongated prefab shells with rounded corners, sturdy raised concrete footings, pale panels and faded teal/orange replacements, external utility connections, little covered porches and modest roof-mounted sensor equipment. Add one inviting workshop with an open shaded work bay, a small clinic/service office, homes with improvised shade canopies, and a communal paved or packed-earth yard. A narrow worn footpath winds from a gap in the foreground vegetation into this yard. Construction clears only small local footprints; most of the forest remains.
Include a compact water-processing/service machine at the settlement edge: two upright filtration tanks, pipe manifolds, a reachable control cabinet and a service platform. Practical crates, one small parked cargo buggy and three residents in ordinary futuristic work clothes communicate everyday life. Subtle warm interior light within shaded openings is allowed, but retain the screenshot's daytime illumination. Distinctly advanced civilian technology with personality, scale and comfort, no military encampment or scrapyard. All new buildings should integrate into the original game rendering rather than upgrading or repainting the whole forest.
